events.title: The last hour
events.text: Seven days of bombardment end in an hour of it. At 6.25 the final barrage begins on the German trenches from Gommecourt to the Somme, 'an incessant roar of gun-fire'. Thirteen British divisions of the Fourth Army and of the Third Army's VII Corps stand in their trenches along 25 km of front, with the French XX Corps on their right. The red lines are the trenches, British and German alike, as the trench maps of the spring drew them.

events.title: Hawthorn Ridge
events.text: At 7.20, ten minutes before zero, the 252nd Tunnelling Company fires 40,000 lb of ammonal under the Hawthorn Ridge Redoubt above Beaumont-Hamel. At the same moment the heavy guns lift off the German front line all along VIII Corps. Most of the 292 men Reserve Infantry Regiment 119 lost that day were under the mine.

events.title: The mines
events.text: At 7.28 the mines go up at La Boisselle and Fricourt: Lochnagar, 60,000 lb, under the German line south of the village; Y Sap, 40,600 lb, at its north-west corner; two of 8,000 lb at the Glory Hole, where no man's land is 50 yards wide; two under the Tambour at Fricourt, a third failing; and Bulgar Point before Mametz. Kasino Point at Carnoy went up at 7.27, late, after the 18th Division's first wave had started.

events.title: Zero
events.text: 'At 7.30 a.m. the crisis came.' The British infantry go over along the whole front, in waves about 100 yards apart, and the French beside them. The barrage lifts off the German front line and moves on, 50 yards a minute on VIII Corps' front. The German garrisons have sat out the bombardment in dugouts 20 to 30 feet deep.

events.title: Gommecourt
events.text: The Third Army's VII Corps attacks the Gommecourt salient from both sides. On the south the 56th (London) Division's leading companies went out to tapes in no man's land under smoke at 7.25, across 800 yards; at 7.30 the London Scottish, Rangers, Queen Victoria's Rifles and London Rifle Brigade rise and break through the first two German trenches, and the third after bombing. On the north the 46th's Staffords reach uncut wire and are shot down; three waves of the 1/5th and 1/7th Sherwood Foresters get into the German front trench, some into the second.

events.title: Serre and the copses
events.text: The 31st Division's Pals battalions walk towards Serre on its knoll, 1,000 yards off. The 15th West Yorkshire, the Leeds Pals, is wiped out. The 11th East Lancashire's right company, from Accrington, gets into the German line; at 8.30 observers report Accrington men in Serre, and at 9.15 an artillery observer sees 80 to 100 men entering the village. The division loses 3,600.

events.title: Beaumont-Hamel
events.text: The 29th Division has 500 yards to cross. Two platoons of the 2nd Royal Fusiliers reach the near lip of the Hawthorn crater; the 1st Lancashire Fusiliers are mown down leaving the Sunken Lane, and 50 men reach the bank beyond; the 2nd South Wales Borderers are destroyed by 7.35 and the 1st Inniskillings killed at the wire of Y Ravine. To the north the 4th Division's 1st Rifle Brigade and 1/8th Warwicks get into the German front trench and the Quadrilateral, while the 1st East Lancashire are stopped by the wire.

events.title: Out of Thiepval Wood
events.text: At 7.15 the 36th (Ulster) Division's 108th and 109th Brigades crept out of Thiepval Wood to within 100 yards of the German line. At 7.30 the buglers sound the advance, and by 7.48 they are in the German B Line with many prisoners; by eight they have overrun the Schwaben Redoubt's front face and are in the German reserve trench, 500 yards beyond the first. Reserve Infantry Regiment 99's centre battalion is destroyed; 500 of its men are taken. North of the Ancre the 108th's other two battalions attack toward Beaucourt station.

events.title: The Leipzig Salient
events.text: At 7.23 the 17th Highland Light Infantry's leading companies left their trench and lay down 30 to 40 yards from the Leipzig Redoubt. At 7.30 they rushed it and took the quarry's garrison, pushed on to Hindenburg Trench and came back. On their left the 16th HLI and 2nd KOYLI are stopped at the Wonderwork's wire, and before Thiepval the 16th Northumberland Fusiliers and the Salford Pals are cut down; 100 Salfords who get into the village are lost.

events.title: Mash Valley: Ovillers
events.text: The 8th Division attacks Ovillers across Mash Valley, 750 yards of open ground. About 200 men of the 23rd Brigade, the 2nd Middlesex and 2nd Devons, reach the German second trench. At 7.50 parties of the 2nd Lincolns are in the German front trench, and they hold 300 yards of it for two hours. On the left the 70th Brigade's 8th KOYLI and 8th York and Lancaster reach the third trench and are cut off.

events.title: Sausage Valley
events.text: The 34th Division goes for La Boisselle in four columns, three battalions deep. The Tyneside Scottish's 21st and 22nd Northumberland Fusiliers cross the Schwabenhöhe, where no man's land is 200 yards wide, and go down Sausage Valley; the 20th and 23rd are shot down in Mash Valley. The Royal Scots drift right onto the Fricourt spur by 7.48, leaving Sausage Redoubt behind them. The Grimsby Chums and 11th Suffolks are held in no man's land, and parties get into the Lochnagar crater. The Tyneside Irish, starting from the Tara-Usna line a mile back, lose 70 per cent before they reach the British front line.

events.title: Fricourt and the Sunken Road
events.text: Two companies of the 10th West Yorkshire get through to Red Cottage at Fricourt's north end; the rest of the battalion is annihilated by the Tambour's guns. It loses 710 men, more than any other battalion that day. North of the village the 21st Division's 64th Brigade crept up in the last five minutes, took the German front and support trenches and 200 prisoners in ten, and is on the Sunken Road, a mile on, at eight. At 7.45 a company of the 7th Green Howards attacks the village unordered and is destroyed.

events.title: Mametz
events.text: The 7th Division attacks Mametz: no man's land is 100 to 200 yards wide, and the village 700 yards uphill. The 9th Devons are stopped at Mansel Copse, and at 7.40 their fourth company is sent in. By 7.45 the 22nd Manchesters and 1st South Staffords are 700 yards on, over Cemetery Trench; at 7.55 the 2nd Gordons are in Shrine Alley, and at eight the Manchesters are in Bucket Trench with parties in Mametz.

events.title: Kasino Point and Montauban
events.text: Kasino Point's mine went up late, at 7.27, as the 18th Division's first wave started. By 7.50 its 53rd and 54th Brigades are in Pommiers Trench. Beside them the 30th Division has crossed 500 yards: at 7.45 the 21st Brigade takes Alt Trench as the barrage lifts, though the 2nd Green Howards lose 200 men to one machine gun, and by 8.35 it is on Glatz Redoubt and in touch with the 89th.

events.title: The French
events.text: On the right the French XX Corps takes Bois Y and Bois Favière 'like clockwork'. At 8.30 the 30th Division finds Dublin Trench empty, with the 3rd Battalion of the French 153rd Infantry in Dublin Redoubt beside it. Curlu, under drumfire since six, is assaulted at nine. South of the Somme, off the map, two more French corps attack at 9.30 and make the day's biggest gain.

events.title: The Newfoundlanders
events.text: At 9.05 the 1st Newfoundland Regiment of the 29th Division's reserve brigade advances alone from St John's Road, 230 metres behind the front line, over the open because the trenches are choked. Most are dead within 15 minutes, around the Danger Tree in no man's land. Of 801 who went forward, 710 are casualties. At 10.05 de Lisle halts the division.

events.title: Munich Trench and Pendant Copse
events.text: VIII Corps signalled at 8.35 to hold back the 4th Division's 10th and 12th Brigades; the order reached them about nine, too late. At 9.30 the 2nd Seaforths and half the 2nd Lancashire Fusiliers swing left under Redan Ridge, cross south of the Quadrilateral and reach Munich Trench, 500 yards beyond the German front; parties of the 2nd Essex and 1st King's Own get to Munich Trench and Pendant Copse. By eleven they are out of bombs and bombed back, and at noon the survivors are in the Quadrilateral.

events.title: Montauban
events.text: At 10.05 the 90th Brigade's 16th and 17th Manchesters and 2nd Royal Scots Fusiliers enter Montauban and find it deserted. At eleven they are in Montauban Alley beyond it with 100 prisoners. Beside them the 18th Division clears Breslau Support and Beetle Alley, and at 10.20 the Loop surrenders to the 8th Norfolks.

events.title: The second position
events.text: The plan gave the 4th Division three and a half hours to reach the German second position; Bapaume, beyond it, is the town in the top right corner. At ten the 36th's 107th Brigade is within 100 yards of the second position at Stuff Redoubt, eight minutes before the barrage lifts, and is repulsed; the corps' order to halt never reaches it. North of the Ancre the attack has failed but for the Quadrilateral; from Thiepval to La Boisselle a few parties hold on; in the south the line is 2 to 3 km forward.

events.title: La Briqueterie
events.text: The heavy guns fired on La Briqueterie, the brickworks east of Montauban, from 11.30. At 12.30 No. 4 Company of the 20th King's attacks it and rushes it at 12.34; the commander of Infantry Regiment 62 is taken with three of his staff. From 1.45 the German guns shell Montauban.

events.title: The crater and Sausage Redoubt
events.text: From one until 3.20 the British guns bombard Sausage Redoubt. The 21st Division's bombers from the north and the 34th's from the Lochnagar crater in the south both fail; the crater party loses 23 of 30. The survivors of the Grimsby Chums and the 11th Suffolks hold the crater, which Reserve Infantry Regiment 110's 4th Company counter-attacked by midday.

events.title: Fricourt attacked
events.text: At 2.30 the 50th Brigade's 7th Green Howards and 7th East Yorkshire attack Fricourt from Wing Corner to the Tambour: 351 casualties in three minutes, and one party reaches a cellar. At the same hour the 7th Division's 20th Manchesters and 1st Royal Welch Fusiliers take the Rectangle and bomb along to Apple Alley.

events.title: Gommecourt retaken
events.text: By four the Germans have retaken the second trench at Gommecourt, and they recover the first by six. The last to get across to the 56th were the Kensingtons and a London Scottish gun about nine; at two the 1/2nd London sent two companies over and they were mown down. On the north side the 46th's attack, set again for 12.15, 1.15, 2.45 and 3.30 as smoke bombs failed to arrive, never went in, and at 3.30 it was called off.

events.title: Thiepval: the 49th
events.text: The 49th Division, the corps reserve, crossed the Ancre to Thiepval Wood from 10.55. At four its 146th Brigade attacks Thiepval and is shot down. At the Schwaben the counter-attacks of Bavarian Reserve Infantry Regiment 8 and Infantry Regiment 180's recruits go in, held up until now by the British guns.

events.title: Mametz falls
events.text: At three Reserve Infantry Regiment 109's battalion headquarters in Mametz was taken and its defence collapsed. At 3.30 the 2nd Warwicks and 8th Devons went forward after half an hour's bombardment, and 200 Germans surrendered from the Shrine and the village. At 4.05 'the whole of Mametz village' is in British hands. R.I.R. 109 loses about 2,100 men that day, 1,625 of them taken prisoner.

events.title: Montauban Alley
events.text: At 5.40 the troops in Loop Trench complete the 18th Division's second objective, and the Royal Berkshires and Norfolks meet at White Trench. The 30th Division holds Montauban Alley beyond the village. Here and at Mametz the British line has gone forward to stay; at 6.45 the German 12th Division is ordered from Bapaume to take the ridge back.

events.title: The Schwaben Redoubt lost
events.text: The counter-attacks on the Schwaben Redoubt began at two. At 6.30 the first battalion of Infantry Regiment 185 arrived; a rush on the redoubt's south-east corner at seven failed. About ten the second battalion arrives and the Ulstermen's garrison withdraws. By 10.30 the redoubt is abandoned; the Germans find about 700 Irish dead in it. By 11.30 the 36th Division is back in its own trenches. It has lost 5,104 men.

events.title: The counter-attack at dawn
events.text: In the night von Below ordered Reserve Infantry Regiment 111 out of Fricourt, and a British patrol finds the village empty about midnight. At three in the morning of 2 July, with the first grey of dawn, the German counter-attack on Montauban goes in on a four-mile front with Reserve Infantry Regiments 51, 38 and 23 of the 12th Reserve Division. By four it has failed with heavy loss.

events.title: The count
events.text: At 5.40 the 8th Division is relieved and withdrawn north-west of Albert. The first day cost the British 57,470 men, 19,240 of them killed or dead of wounds. The French lost 1,590 and took about 4,500 prisoners; the Germans lost perhaps 10,000 to 12,000. The line had gone forward on a front of 3½ miles, to a mile deep. Of the villages that were the day's objectives Mametz and Montauban fell, and Fricourt in the night; Gommecourt, Serre, Beaumont-Hamel, Thiepval, Ovillers and La Boisselle held out. The Thiepval Memorial, built in 1932 near the château's site, bears 72,246 names, nine in ten of them from the Battle of the Somme.

outcome.result: No breakthrough. In the south Mametz and Montauban were taken and the Germans left Fricourt in the night; north of the Albert to Bapaume road only the Leipzig Redoubt and the Quadrilateral were still held at nightfall
losses: 57,470 on 1 July (the Third and Fourth Armies), of whom 19,240 were killed or died of wounds, in Edmonds's corrected figure; his first count from the diaries was 61,816. By division: the 34th 6,380, the 4th 5,752, the 29th 5,240, the 8th 5,121, the 36th 5,104, the 56th 4,314, the 21st 4,256, the 32nd 3,949, the 31st 3,600, the 7th 3,380, the 18th 3,115, the 30th 3,011, the 46th 2,445, the 50th Brigade 1,155, the 49th 590. The 10th West Yorkshire lost 710 and the Newfoundlanders 710 of 801. The British took 25 officers and 1,958 men prisoner.
The Sixth Army lost 1,590 and took about 4,500 prisoners north and south of the river.

10,000 to 12,000 on 1 July, a modern estimate; the losses were never counted for the day alone. R.I.R. 109 lost about 2,100 (1,625 prisoners or missing), B.R.I.R. 6 1,761 to 1,810, I.R. 62 737, R.I.R. 119 292, I.R. 180 273, and the Gommecourt garrison 1,241.
outcome.note: Clock times are the British and French clock, GMT+1; German accounts give the attack at 8.30, an hour later.
